tips.tip: Tell a trusted friend where you're going, who you're meeting, and when you expect to be back before any first date.
Meet in a public place for the first few dates, and never have someone you just met pick you up from your home.
Keep control of your own transport so you can leave the moment something feels off.
If she asks for money before you've even met in person, it's a scam. No exceptions.
Never send gift cards, crypto, or wire transfers to someone you've only talked to online.
A profile with only model-perfect photos and no normal candid shots is worth a second look.
If she always has an excuse not to video call, you may not be talking to who you think you are.
Do a quick reverse image search on her photos if something feels too polished to be real.
Watch for a story that keeps changing. Real people stay consistent about their own lives.
If the conversation suddenly turns into a crypto or investment opportunity, it was never about you.
Never send explicit photos to someone you don't know and trust. They can become blackmail.
If someone threatens to leak your private photos unless you pay, stop paying, don't delete anything, and report it.
Paying a blackmailer almost never ends it. It just proves you'll pay again.
You are the victim in a sextortion scam, not the one who should feel ashamed. Report it.
Keep your home address, workplace, and daily routine private until trust is genuinely earned.
Trust patterns, not potential. If her words and actions don't match, believe the actions.
Love bombing early on, soulmate talk within days, is a pattern, not proof of real feeling.
If she pushes to move off the app to WhatsApp or Telegram within minutes, slow down and stay cautious.
Guard your drink on dates and never leave it unattended. Drink spiking happens to men too.
If she picks an expensive venue and leaves right after the bill, you may have been set up.
Trust your gut. If something feels wrong, you don't owe anyone an explanation for leaving.
A woman who respects you will respect your 'no' without guilt-tripping or sulking.
Watch how she treats waiters and strangers. That's how she'll eventually treat you.
Don't ignore how she reacts when she doesn't get her way early on. It only intensifies later.
If she rushes you toward big commitments like moving in or lending money, ask who benefits from the rush.
Keep your passwords, bank details, and accounts to yourself no matter how close you feel.
Never co-sign a loan, lease, or anything financial for someone you've been dating a short time.
If she asks to borrow money repeatedly and never pays it back, that's a pattern, not a rough patch.
Limit how much you drink on a first date so you stay aware and in control of your decisions.
If her friends or your friends warn you about her, don't dismiss it just because you're into her.
A sudden emergency that needs money, right after you connect, is one of the oldest scams there is.
If she claims to be stuck abroad and needs cash to get home, it's a textbook romance scam.
Verify she's real with a live video call before you invest serious time or feelings.
If she avoids every attempt to meet in person for weeks, question whether she exists at all.
Screenshot and save any threats, harassment, or blackmail. Don't delete the evidence.
Don't share screenshots of your private conversations with people who might use them against you.
If she goes through your phone and gets angry at what she doesn't find, that's control, not love.
Someone who isolates you from your friends and family is not protecting the relationship, they're trapping you.
If she threatens to hurt herself every time you try to leave, that's manipulation, and you may need outside help.
If she threatens to make false accusations against you, take screenshots and talk to someone you trust.
Men get abused too. If she hits you or threatens you, it's not something to brush off.
Constant insults disguised as jokes are still disrespect. Don't train yourself to accept them.
If she's extremely jealous of every woman you talk to, that's insecurity turning into control.
If she only reaches out when she's drunk, bored, or needs something, you're an option, not a priority.
Don't ignore it when she's warm one day and cold the next. Inconsistency is the message.
Someone who guilt-trips you for prioritizing your safety is already showing you who they are.
If she mocks your gut instinct or calls you paranoid, she'd rather you doubt yourself than question her.
You don't owe a second chance to someone who made you feel unsafe the first time.
If she says she's not looking for anything serious but acts like your girlfriend, believe her words.
Be cautious if she only ever wants to meet at your place and never anywhere public.
Don't hand over your car, keys, or apartment access to someone you've known a few weeks.
If she claims to be pregnant very soon after you meet, stay calm and ask for proof before any decision.
If you find out she has a boyfriend or husband, walk away before it becomes your problem.
A woman who respects herself won't ask you to lie to or betray the people close to you.
If early conversations are all about your job, income, and what you own, notice what she's really interested in.
Keep some emotional distance until you actually know someone. Vulnerability given too early can be used.
Don't tell a near-stranger your deepest insecurities. Let trust be earned before you hand over ammunition.
If she keeps bringing up money problems and hinting you should solve them, that's a setup, not a struggle.
Be wary of anyone who love bombs you, pulls away, then love bombs again to keep you hooked.
If you feel like you're walking on eggshells to avoid her anger, that's a red flag, not a personality quirk.
Take it seriously if she tries to control what you wear, who you see, or how you spend your time.
A partner who punishes you with silence every time you disagree is using control, not communication.
If she flips every argument into your fault until you apologize for things you didn't do, step back and think clearly.
Don't let flattery switch off your judgment. Scammers and manipulators lead with compliments.
If a match seems too perfect, too interested, too fast, slow down and pay closer attention.
Keep early dates short and low-stakes until you know the person is who they say they are.
Tell someone your exact plan for any first meet, including the venue and what time to check on you.
If she insists on keeping your relationship secret with no real reason, ask yourself why.
Don't invest months into someone who refuses to meet, call, or confirm basic facts about themselves.
If she asks for your Social Security number, ID photos, or banking info, that's identity theft bait.
Be careful what personal info you post publicly. Scammers study your profile to seem compatible.
If she mirrors every single interest of yours perfectly, it may be a tactic, not a coincidence.
Someone who creates urgency and panic around decisions is trying to stop you from thinking.
Don't meet anyone in a remote or private location you've never been to for a first date.
If she gets aggressive when you set a simple boundary, imagine that reaction on a bigger issue.
Keep your own friendships and hobbies alive. A partner who wants all your time is a warning sign.
If she's constantly testing you with jealousy games, that behavior won't disappear once you commit.
Don't confuse intensity for compatibility. Chaos and drama aren't the same as chemistry.
If she asks you to keep secrets from your family that make you uneasy, trust that discomfort.
A person who respects you won't pressure you into anything physical before you're ready.
If she pressures you about sex and sulks or punishes you when you're not ready, that's a red flag.
Watch for someone who's charming in public but cold or cruel the moment you're alone.
If her stories about her past never quite add up, don't explain away the inconsistencies.
Don't lend your car, your money, or your name to impress someone early in dating.
If she only shows interest right after you pull back, she may be managing you, not liking you.
Believe someone the first time they show you cruelty, not the tenth time you forgive it.
If she posts cryptic things about you online during every disagreement, that's a manipulation habit.
Keep copies of anything important. If a relationship turns ugly, documentation protects you.
If you feel worse about yourself the more time you spend with her, pay attention to that.
A healthy partner adds to your life. If someone constantly drains it, that's information.
Don't ignore friends who say you've changed or seem smaller since you started seeing her.
If she keeps a running scoreboard of your mistakes to use against you, that's control.
Never feel obligated to continue a date that feels wrong. Pay, leave, and protect your peace.
If she asks you to delete or hide the conversation from your own future self, the relationship is already crossing lines.
Scammers rely on loneliness. The harder someone pushes fast love, the more you should slow down.
If she won't let you tell anyone about the relationship, that secrecy usually protects her, not you.
Don't make major life changes, quitting a job, moving cities, for someone you barely know.
If a connection moves from flirting to financial requests, that's the whole point of it.
Your safety and self-respect come first. No connection is worth ignoring your own alarm bells.
If leaving feels scary because of how she might react, that fear itself is telling you something important.
If she talks about her exes as all crazy or all abusive, notice that she's the common thread in every story.
A woman who brags about making men chase or spend on her is telling you how she sees relationships.
If she keeps score of who texted last and plays games with it, expect games in everything else too.
Watch if she only lights up when you're buying, planning, or paying, and goes flat otherwise.
If her mood toward you rises and falls with your usefulness, you're a resource, not a partner.
A woman who never apologizes and always reframes her mistakes as your fault won't change later.
If she tests you with little traps to catch you slipping, she's looking for reasons, not connection.
Notice if she flirts with other men right in front of you to keep you insecure. That's deliberate.
If she compares you to other guys to make you work harder, she's managing you, not choosing you.
A woman who threatens to leave every time she wants something is using fear as a tool.
If she disappears for days then returns like nothing happened, she's keeping you on a leash.
Watch for someone who's sweet until you commit, then stops trying the moment she feels secure.
If she can't go one conversation without mentioning money, gifts, or lifestyle, notice the priority.
A woman who expects you to fund her life while giving little back sees you as a wallet.
If she gets cold the second you stop spending, the warmth was never really about you.
Watch if she hides her phone, flips it over constantly, or gets defensive about simple questions.
If she's still 'just friends' with exes who clearly want more, and hides it, pay attention.
A woman who lies about small, pointless things will lie about big ones when it matters.
If her age, job, or relationship status online doesn't match reality, that's deliberate deception.
Watch for someone who's a completely different person in public than she is with you alone.
If she belittles your job, your car, or your income as not enough, she's showing you her values.
A woman who mocks you in front of her friends isn't teasing, she's establishing who's above who.
If she dismisses everything you care about as boring or stupid, she doesn't respect you.
Watch if she expects constant attention but offers almost none in return.
If she punishes you with the silent treatment instead of talking, that's control, not communication.
A woman who brings up your past mistakes in every argument is building a weapon, not fixing a problem.
If she never asks a single question about your life, your interest is one-sided.
Watch for someone who makes every conversation about herself and tunes out when it's your turn.
If she only texts back when she's bored and ignores you when she's busy, you're a backup.
A woman who sends you to voicemail then posts online all night is telling you where you rank.
If she needs constant validation from other men online, that need won't stop because you're dating.
Watch if she measures love by how much you spend rather than how you treat her.
If she guilt-trips you for seeing your friends or family, she's isolating you slowly.
A woman who tries to pick your friends and cut off the ones she dislikes is controlling, not caring.
If she escalates small disagreements into huge fights, drama may be the point for her.
Watch for someone who threatens self-harm to stop you from leaving or setting a boundary.
If she accuses you of cheating with no evidence, constantly, that projection is worth noticing.
A woman who goes through your messages and twists innocent things into betrayal is looking for conflict.
If she love bombs you hard and fast, then grows cold, that cycle rarely gets better.
Watch if she rushes 'I love you' or future plans before she even knows you. It's often a hook.
If she talks about marriage and kids on date one, slow down and watch whether it's about you or a timeline.
A woman who tries to get you to quit your job, move, or change your life fast benefits from the rush.
If she keeps other guys on standby as backups and calls it 'just friends,' believe the pattern.
Watch for someone who's on dating apps active and messaging while telling you you're exclusive.
If she blames all her problems on everyone else and never herself, you'll be blamed too eventually.
A woman who's rude to waiters, drivers, and staff is showing you her real character.
If she treats people who can't do anything for her badly, that's who she actually is.
Watch if she's obsessed with status, brands, and appearances over substance and kindness.
If she looks down on your family or friends for having less, notice what she truly values.
A woman who expects you to drop everything for her but never does the same keeps the scales tilted.
If she cancels on you constantly but expects you to always be available, that's imbalance by design.
Watch for someone who only reaches out when she needs a favor, a ride, or money.
If she makes you feel guilty for having needs or wanting clarity, she's dodging accountability.
A woman who refuses to define the relationship for months while enjoying all the benefits is stalling on purpose.
If she keeps you a secret from her friends and family with no real reason, ask yourself why.
Watch if she introduces you as 'just a friend' long after things should be clear.
If her stories about her day keep contradicting each other, the truth is probably somewhere else.
A woman who flips from affection to cruelty quickly is showing you an unstable pattern, not passion.
If she withholds affection as punishment and gives it as reward, she's training you, not loving you.
Watch for someone who makes you apologize for feelings you're allowed to have.
If she gaslights you into doubting what you clearly saw or heard, take that seriously.
A woman who says 'you're too sensitive' every time she hurts you is avoiding responsibility.
If she only respects you when you push back and walks over you when you're kind, that's a bad dynamic.
Watch if she expects grand gestures but calls your everyday effort not enough.
If nothing you do is ever sufficient and the goalposts keep moving, you're in a losing game.
A woman who compares your relationship to others to shame you into more is manipulating, not sharing.
If she uses sex as a reward or punishment to control your behavior, notice the pattern.
Watch for someone who threatens to cheat or flirts openly to keep you anxious.
If she enjoys making you jealous and then denies doing it, that's a game, not a misunderstanding.
A woman who never takes accountability and always plays the victim will never see her own part.
If every ex 'did her wrong' and she did nothing, the odds say you'll be the next villain.
Watch if she pressures you into decisions fast so you don't have time to think.
If she's offended that you want to take things slow, ask what the hurry is really about.
A woman who lies about where she's been and gets angry you asked is hiding something.
If she picks fights right before you have plans with others, she may be sabotaging on purpose.
Watch for someone who tracks your location, demands constant check-ins, and calls it love.
If she needs to know your every move and panics when she can't reach you, that's control.
A woman who reads your texts and dictates who you can talk to has crossed into control.
If she makes you prove your loyalty with tests and sacrifices, you'll never pass for long.
Watch if she brings up other men's interest to make you feel replaceable.
If she keeps a 'just in case' guy around for attention and gifts, you're sharing her focus.
A woman who's warm in private but pretends she barely knows you in public may be hiding you.
If she's embarrassed by you around her friends, that's not nerves, it's how she sees you.
Watch for someone who expects you to change your personality to fit her image of a boyfriend.
If she tries to mold you into someone else, she didn't actually want the man she met.
A woman who criticizes your appearance, weight, or style constantly is chipping at your confidence.
If she makes 'jokes' about your insecurities she knows about, that's cruelty, not humor.
Watch if she shares your private struggles with her friends and laughs about them.
If she betrays small confidences, bigger ones aren't safe with her either.
A woman who's addicted to drama and starts it when things get calm will never let it stay peaceful.
If peace feels boring to her and she keeps creating chaos, that's a pattern, not a phase.
Watch for someone who's generous with promises and empty on follow-through.
If she says all the right things but her actions never match, trust the actions.
A woman who future-fakes trips and plans she never intends to keep is managing your hope.
If she dangles commitment to keep you invested but never delivers, that's a tactic.
Watch if she only becomes interested again the moment you start to move on.
If she reappears every time you pull away but vanishes when you're close, she wants the leash, not you.
A woman who can't be happy for your wins and competes with you instead isn't on your team.
If she resents your success or friendships, that envy will quietly poison the relationship.
Watch for someone who makes you feel you need permission to have a life of your own.
If you've stopped doing things you love just to keep her calm, notice how much you've given up.
A woman who weaponizes your kindness and takes it as weakness will keep taking.
If being generous and patient gets you walked on, she's not someone worth that generosity.
Watch if she's affectionate only when she wants something and distant the rest of the time.
If her warmth is a transaction, you'll always be paying to feel wanted.
A woman who refuses to meet in a normal public setting and insists on secrecy online may be hiding her real life.
If her online persona feels scripted and polished but she dodges spontaneous questions, be cautious.
Watch for a match who mirrors you perfectly, agrees with everything, and has no edges of her own.
If she seems to want exactly what you want within days, that may be a tactic, not compatibility.
A woman whose photos never change, never show daily life, and never include friends is worth questioning.
If she won't send a casual real-time photo or do a quick video, something may be off.
Watch if she steers every chat toward how lonely, broke, or desperate she is. That's often a setup.
If she escalates emotional intimacy online faster than any real person would, slow down.
A woman who gets angry when you want to verify basic facts about her is hiding something.
If she refuses to meet for months with endless excuses, you may be feeding a fantasy.
Watch for someone who suddenly has a crisis the moment you seem ready to meet in person.
If her 'emergencies' always appear right when the relationship should take a real step, notice the timing.
A woman who tells you not to trust your friends' opinions of her is isolating you early.
If she turns you against the people who care about you, that's a tactic, not loyalty.
Watch if she rewrites history and insists arguments went differently than they did.
If you start recording details just to prove your own memory, that's a warning sign.
A woman who makes you feel crazy for noticing real patterns is counting on your self-doubt.
If she calls your valid concerns 'insecurity' to shut you up, don't let it work.
Watch for someone who expects total transparency from you but total privacy for herself.
If the rules apply to you and never to her, that double standard won't balance out.
A woman who shames you for crying or opening up will make you bottle everything until it breaks.
If vulnerability gets used against you later, you've learned something important about her.
Watch if she keeps you anxious on purpose, hot then cold, so you never feel secure.
If calm and certainty seem to bore her, she may be addicted to the anxiety she creates.
A woman who treats your boundaries as challenges to overcome doesn't respect them.
If every 'no' you give becomes a negotiation, your limits don't mean anything to her yet.
Watch for someone who expects you to read her mind and punishes you for guessing wrong.
If she refuses to say what she wants but holds it against you, that's a no-win setup.
A woman who's generous with criticism and stingy with appreciation will wear you down.
If you can't remember the last time she thanked or praised you, notice the imbalance.
Watch if she only commits when there's an audience and backs off in private.
If she's your girlfriend on social media but not in real life, the post isn't the truth.
A woman who hints at other men's money or looks to pressure you is playing a comparison game.
If she makes you feel you must outbid some invisible rival, step back and see the manipulation.
Watch for someone who's charming when things go her way and vicious the moment they don't.
If her kindness has a short fuse the second she's inconvenienced, that temper is the real her.
A woman who refuses to ever be wrong will make sure you're always the one apologizing.
If arguments only end when you give in, you're keeping the peace by disappearing.
Watch if she expects you to prove yourself endlessly while she risks nothing.
If you're always auditioning and she's always judging, that's not a partnership.
A woman who's quick to involve exes, make you jealous, or stir rivalry thrives on chaos.
If she enjoys the tension more than the peace, that won't change once you commit.
Watch for someone who reveals cruelty early, then love bombs you to make you forget it.
If the sweetness always arrives right after the cruelty, that cycle is the relationship.
A woman who makes you feel lucky just to be tolerated has flipped the dynamic against you.
If you're grateful for scraps of attention, your standards have quietly been lowered.
Watch if she only respects strength and punishes kindness. That's a dynamic that will exhaust you.
If being a good man gets you walked on while being distant gets her interest, she's not your match.
A woman worth your time will meet your effort, respect your boundaries, and be consistent. If she won't, believe her.
